# ISSUE-270 implementation plan

Extract ExecuteWork into a private per-invocation state and named phase methods. This is a mechanical refactor: retain every operation, branch, message, public API, and observable ordering. Approved dimensions are multi_area / known / sensitive; use independent review and existing adversarial coverage. Estimated plan, implementation, and validation: 6–10 hours within the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- ExecuteWork spans engine.go:496–1295. Its nine shared-state closures start at 690, 716, 729, 751, 770, 776, 803, 1016, and 1192.
- Setup acquires/resumes the claim before installing the setup-release defer (engine.go:551–580), starts heartbeat at 631, and completes provisioning at 683. Early returns before a result exists return nil.
- Budget admission and interruption defers are installed only after result initialization (engine.go:702–715); their registration order matters. Coordinator operations retain the caller context while agents use heartbeat.Context() (631, 689).
- preserveRejected snapshots the worktree head when building the callback, not when invoking it (729–750). checkImport reads the current state at callback invocation (716–728).
- Developer and validation rounds already fit below 200 lines (1016–1189 and 1192–1259). The repair loop is 1260–1292. Preflight is 309–466; the other existing engine functions fit the requested bound by source inspection.
- Existing tests cover gates, stale fences, import recovery, budget interruption, repair limits, and split termination; references and commands are below. Makefile:check runs lint and race tests across the repository.
- The slash-command definition .claude/commands/swarm-plan.md requests these two artifacts only. Production sources and existing tests remain untouched during planning.

## What we're assuming

- A per-run state can preserve closure semantics without introducing synchronization: retain existing synchronous execution and callback lifetimes; confirm with focused race tests and independent review.
- Proposed execute_*.go files are absent in this snapshot (directory listing checked). This snapshot has no .git metadata, and workunit.json provides no approved base SHA. Before implementation, the coordinator/developer must confirm absence against the authoritative approved base using git ls-tree, and record its SHA. If any exists there, treat it as modified and reconcile its contents before extraction.

## Open questions

- Will extraction expose a coverage gap in deferred cleanup or callback timing? Resolve through the independent comparison and adversarial suites; if needed add a separate new regression test file without changing existing tests.
- Approved-base filename and provenance confirmation, plus final PR-body verification, require the coordinator's Git checkout. These are handoff verification items, not requests for agent credentials or blockers on drafting the implementation.

## Design and exact touchpoints

Modify only internal/workflow/engine.go and add the following files, subject to the approved-base absence check. Keep existing helper implementations, WorkOptions, WorkResult, public signatures, and internal/pr unchanged.

- execute_run.go: private workRun type; check, checkImport, preserveRejected, rejectImport, pauseInterrupted, admit, stopForSplit; deferred helpers finishProgress, releaseFailedSetup, stopHeartbeat, finishAdmission, finishInterrupted.
- execute_setup.go: setup, preflightRun, claimRun, loadClaimPolicy, startHeartbeat, resumeForkCheckpoint, provisionWorkspace, initializeResult.
- execute_plan.go: plan and finishPlanHandoff.
- execute_review.go: reviewGate, awaitHumanReview, runReview, finishReviewHandoff.
- execute_implementation.go: prepareImplementation, developerRound.
- execute_validation.go: validationRound, validateAndRepair, finish.

workRun holds engine, normalized options, caller/coordinator context, heartbeat-derived run context, progress, preflight result, duration, claim state, approved config/workflow, dependencies, gate, resumed/setup-complete flags, heartbeat, fork settings, worktree/branch, result, active phase/checkpoint preservation, mode, implementation base, runPlan, rejected-plan context, repair limit/rerun text and outcomeFailed. Use existing concrete types (lease.Heartbeat and sandbox.Dependencies included); avoid new exported APIs or engine-global state. Keep ordinary phase-local temporaries local. Phase methods return (done bool, err error) when they can terminate normally; do not infer termination from result fields. Round methods retain their existing paused/error contract.

Callback factories may still return signature adapters required by RunRequest, but move their policy logic to methods. Preserve per-callback head snapshot in a private rejectedRunSnapshot value with a named preserve method; do not replace it with mutable shared snapshot state. checkImport's adapter must dereference current workRun state. No generic phase framework or unrelated cleanup.

## Implementation sequence and original-source ledger

1. Record the approved base SHA and line-numbered original engine.go. Establish baseline focused tests. Verify proposed filenames at that base. Save the extraction ledger for the PR description, extending the mapping below to every actual new function, including adapters and any further helpers.
2. Introduce workRun and move shared state mechanically. Keep ExecuteWork named returns and explicit result propagation. Register cleanup at the original milestones: progress first; failed-setup release after successful acquire/resume; heartbeat stop after startup; admission conversion then interruption conversion after result initialization. LIFO execution must remain interruption → admission → heartbeat → release → progress. A setup helper must not defer heartbeat stop or successful-setup cleanup to its own return.
3. Extract setup in order using these original ranges: preflightRun 509–545; claimRun 546–590; loadClaimPolicy 591–629; startHeartbeat 630–642; resumeForkCheckpoint 643–665; provisionWorkspace 666–682; initializeResult 683–689 and 782–802. setup orchestrates these ranges with cleanup registration left at the exact milestones. Do not move evidence writes ahead of budget-defer installation.
4. Extract check 690–701, finishAdmission 702–709, finishInterrupted 710–715, checkImport 716–728, preserveRejected/snapshot callback 729–750, rejectImport 751–769, pauseInterrupted 770–775, admit 776–781, stopForSplit 803–810. Preserve error wrapping and checks exactly. Map finishProgress to 497–508 and releaseFailedSetup to 566–573; stopHeartbeat comes from 632.
5. Extract plan 811–925, with finishPlanHandoff from 906–923; reviewGate orchestrates 926–989, awaitHumanReview 929–953, runReview 954–989 and finishReviewHandoff 974–986. Verify precise brace boundaries against the saved source before moving; overlapping ranges identify delegation. Preserve the second split check and all original phase predicates, including runPlan's meaning after planning completes.
6. Extract prepareImplementation 990–1015, developerRound 1016–1189, validationRound 1192–1259, validateAndRepair 1260–1292, and finish 1293–1294. Keep initial implementation skipping, trusted report precedence, repair-round counters, approved-base limits, PR/fork checkpoint branches, and no-change diagnostics intact.
7. Reduce ExecuteWork to at most 120 physical lines of lifecycle setup and explicit phase calls. Keep every function in engine.go and added files at most 200 physical lines after gofmt. Split only at contiguous boundaries if a limit is exceeded; record each resulting function in the provenance ledger. Avoid formatting compression to meet the limits.
8. Run TEST_PLAN.md checks. Require independent review through the approved agent gate and independent implementation review comparing original/new operation order, fences, contexts, cleanup, and callbacks. Fix discrepancies by preserving original behavior, never by changing existing test assertions. Prepare the PR description's complete function-to-original-range table for the coordinator's explicit publication step.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved policy or gates.

- Entry points: engine.go:496 ExecuteWork; :690 check; :716 checkImport; :729 preserveRejected; :751 rejectImport; :770 pauseInterrupted; :776 admit; :803 stopForSplit; :1016 developerRound; :1192 validationRound. New-method provenance starts with the ledger above; use the approved original, not post-extraction line numbers.
- Extend no existing test files. Reuse engine_test.go:24/210/338/484/584/707, work_validation_test.go:285/390/413/465/509, claim_budget_test.go:83/194/233/361, import_policy_test.go:129/195/413, split_recommendation_test.go:139/230/275, recovery_test.go:18, recorded_branch_test.go:16 and their existing fixtures. Add a new test file only if a concrete missing regression warrants it.
- Exact focused commands: `go test -race ./internal/workflow/... ./internal/cli/...`; adversarial subset and full checks are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: filesystem listing shows no execute_*.go files; source confirms callback snapshot timing, two contexts, cleanup ordering, and current round lengths; Makefile confirms make check includes repository-wide race tests. Tests were not run during artifact-only planning.
- Reopen the plan if preserving behavior requires changing public APIs, protected files, existing tests, internal/pr, execution ordering, or scope beyond this extraction; also reopen if projected work exceeds the claim budget.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search finds ExecuteWork callers in internal/cli/work.go:142, internal/cli/node.go:193 and existing workflow tests: preserve unchanged. WorkOptions/WorkResult, progress stages, agent prompts, errors, artifacts, and JSON consumers: preserve unchanged. Existing helper callers and internal/pr: preserve unchanged. No docs/templates require updates because no public behavior changes. Original engine.go source line references become stale after extraction; update the PR provenance table to name every destination function while retaining approved-original ranges. Existing test names and assertions remain unchanged.

# ISSUE-270 test plan

Use the approved baseline in a Git-equipped coordinator checkout for diffs and original-source comparisons. This planning snapshot lacks Git metadata. Do not change existing test files. Planning produces artifacts only; test results below must be collected during implementation/validation.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Verification |
| --- | --- |
| ExecuteWork ≤ about 120 lines; every function in engine.go and new files ≤ about 200; named phases | After gofmt, use a temporary Go parser-based checker (outside production source) using go/parser and token.FileSet: for each FuncDecl compute End line minus Pos line plus one; include function literals in the scan as well. Fail above 120 for ExecuteWork and 200 for every other function in the specified files. Review ExecuteWork for explicit setup, plan, review, implementation, validation/repair, finish calls and early termination. |
| Nine closures become methods/small functions with explicit run state | Inspect declarations and all former captures against original engine.go:690–810, 1016–1259; confirm workRun owns shared state, no Engine-global run state, callbacks read current claim state, and recovery snapshot remains per-run-call. Run existing lifecycle/adversarial/race tests below. |
| Focused race suite and make check pass; existing tests unchanged | Run the exact required commands below. `git diff --exit-code "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA" -- ':(glob)**/*_test.go'` must be empty for existing files; when adding a justified new regression file, separately compare only test paths tracked at the approved base. Check staged and unstaged changes against the base, not just working-tree changes. |
| PR description lists every new function and its original line range | Review the coordinator-prepared PR body against the complete added FuncDecl/function-literal inventory. Each destination function includes approved-original engine.go range(s), including orchestration, cleanup helpers and callback adapters. Verify ranges with `git show "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA:internal/workflow/engine.go"` and line-numbered original output. Artifact preparation is local; final published-body verification belongs to create_pr, not this sandbox. |

Set APPROVED_BASE_SHA from authoritative claim/WorkUnit metadata; never guess it from the candidate HEAD.

## Focused behavior and adversarial checks

```bash
go test -race ./internal/workflow/... -run 'Test(EnginePlanGateLifecycle|CollaborativeHandoffAndDecomposition|ReviewPhaseHandoff|EngineSetupProgressSharedSessionBundles|EngineRoleHandoffs|ProviderFailureResume|ExecuteWorkTitleEditRecordedBranch|EngineDroppedCheckpointRecovery)$'
go test -race ./internal/workflow/... -run 'Test(WorkValidationRepairRounds|WorkRepairLimitComesFromApprovedBase|WorkRepairStaleWorkerFailsWithClaimFence|WorkRepairPausesNearClaimBudget|WorkRepairRejectsForgedActiveFiles|BudgetPauseCheckpointsAndResumes|BudgetPauseStillRequiresFence|BudgetPauseDuringRequiredChecksDoesNotRecordFailure|BudgetCleanupExpiryDuringHandoffRemainsFenceError|ImportRejectionRecovery|TesterReadsApprovedInputs|DeletionCheckUsesTrustedState|ExecuteWorkStopsOnSplitRecommendation|SplitRecommendationCannotSkipRequiredGate|SplitRecommendationRequiresTheClaim)$'
go test -race ./internal/workflow/... ./internal/cli/...
```

The first command exercises phase gates, setup progress, handoffs, failure/resume and branch recovery. The second exercises stale worker errors, cancellation/claim-budget cleanup, approved-base repair limits, forged inputs, rejected imports and split termination. Inspect subtest results and skips; a skipped boundary is not passing evidence for that boundary. Full package suites additionally cover policy changes, dependency preparation, implementation outcomes and CLI output.

Independent reviewer compares operation sequences against the original, especially nil result on setup failure; acquire versus resume release; LIFO defers; caller versus heartbeat contexts; import rejection before budget handling; human/agent/no gate predicates; repeated split checks; implementation evidence reuse; PR and fork checkpoint fencing; and trusted-validation precedence. Preserve all `%w` chains so errors.Is still detects ErrClaimFence and other sentinels. No new behavior or security fix is planned; if review finds an extraction regression not covered by existing tests, add a focused regression in a new test file and confirm it fails on the faulty extraction.

## Required repository checks

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

These cover the compiled required checks and the WorkUnit's explicit make check requirement. Use writable build caches supplied by the sandbox. Record environmental failures and skips accurately; do not edit policies, weaken tests, request coordinator credentials, or claim unavailable checks passed. Installation is unnecessary for this private refactor and is not supported by this sandbox's writable roots.

## Diff and provenance review

```bash
git diff --check
git diff --name-status "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA"
git diff --exit-code "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA" -- ':(glob)**/*_test.go'
git show "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA:internal/workflow/engine.go" > /tmp/issue-270-original-engine.go
```

Confirm production changes are restricted to engine.go and the planned new workflow files, aside from a specifically justified new regression file; no existing test changes or renames. Before extraction, use `git ls-tree -r --name-only "$APPROVED_BASE_SHA" -- internal/workflow` to confirm every proposed new filename is absent, relabeling existing paths as modifications if necessary. The independent reviewer signs off on provenance completeness and behavior preservation; the coordinator records actual command results and completes the existing approved gates.
